name: Watershed Assistance Grant Program
summary: Grants for the design and permitting of watershed restoration projects (stream, wetland and shoreline restoration, stormwater practices) and for watershed planning in Maryland, the West Virginia Chesapeake watershed and parts of Pennsylvania. Funds early project phases, not construction.

geography.label: Maryland, West Virginia Chesapeake watershed, parts of Pennsylvania

amount.note: Design up to $100,000 for stormwater and similar practices, up to $150,000 for stream, wetland and living shoreline design; planning up to $75,000

eligibility.rule: Project is in Maryland, the WV Chesapeake watershed, or the Octoraro or Conowingo Creek watersheds (PA)
For Pennsylvania projects, align with the Conowingo Watershed Implementation Plan
Comply with federal employment and non-discrimination laws
Have no listed debarment, fraud-related conviction or termination for cause or default
Complete the project within 12 to 16 months of receiving the award
For stream restoration designs, use licensed or registered professionals

documents: Letter of Commitment from each project partner, if provided
Written landowner confirmation, if the applicant does not own the project property
Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA), if applicable

status.quote: Program Status: OPEN Deadline: Wednesday, December 9th, 2026, at 4:00 PM EST

deadline.quote: Program Status: OPEN Deadline: Wednesday, December 9th, 2026, at 4:00 PM EST

applicant_types.quote: Municipal, County, and Regional Agencies Nonprofit Organizations Faith-based Organizations Community and Homeowners Associations (HOAs) Soil/Water Conservation Districts & Resource Conservation and Development Councils Forestry Boards Public and Independent Higher Educational Institutions

geography.quote: All communities in Maryland, throughout the Chesapeake Bay watershed in West Virginia, and the Pennsylvania portions of the Octoraro and Conowingo Creek Watersheds are eligible.

access.quote: Program Status: OPEN Deadline: Wednesday, December 9th, 2026, at 4:00 PM EST

amount.quote: Generally, requests are up to $150,000 for design of Stream restoration practices, Wetland and marsh creation/restoration projects, and Living shorelines.

co_finance_required.quote: Match is encouraged but not required.

window.quote: Program Status: OPEN Deadline: Wednesday, December 9th, 2026, at 4:00 PM EST

effort.quote: Applicants must submit applications through the Chesapeake Bay Trust Awards Portal by 4:00 PM EST on December 9, 2026.
The TRC reviews and scores all applications based on the criteria listed in the "Evaluation Criteria" section above, then meets to discuss application merits and develop funding recommendations.

eligibility.quote: all applicants must be a 501(c)(3) to be eligible for funding
All communities in Maryland, throughout the Chesapeake Bay watershed in West Virginia, and the Pennsylvania portions of the Octoraro and Conowingo Creek Watersheds are eligible.

These projects must align with the goals of the Conowingo Watershed Implementation Plan (CWIP), a cross-jurisdictional collaboration to address additional nutrient and sediment loads resulting from Conowingo Reservoir infill.
they are compliant with federal employment and non-discrimination laws

they have not been debarred, convicted, charged or had a civil judgment rendered against them for fraud or related offense by any government agency (federal, state or local) or been terminated for cause or default by any government agency (federal, state, or local).
Projects must be completed within 12 to 16 months of receipt of the award.
Designs shall be done by licensed/registered professionals.

after_award.quote: If approved, the Trust will send an award agreement with award conditions and due dates of status, progress, and final reports.

documents.quote: Applicants are encouraged to upload a Letter of Commitment for the project from each partner describing in detail the partner's role or contribution to the project.

Applicants proposing work on property they do not own should include written landowner confirmation authorizing access for field investigations and design activities and acknowledging anticipated access needs for future construction if the project advances to implementation.
If you have a Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA), it must be uploaded with the application.
